items.berryRestockNote: After a battle, the first of these the bag holds goes into an empty hand.
items.berryRecommendNote: Fills the order for the companion walking now: healing, then halving a hit it is weak to, then a stat boost.
items.berryAutoNote: When on and none of the three choices is in the bag, an empty hand takes whichever berry suits the companion best: halving a 4× weakness, then healing, then halving a 2× weakness, then a stat boost, then a status cure.
items.healingUseNote: Thrown in place of the turn it is thrown on. The Bag button throws one by hand.
items.healingAutoNote: The smallest that covers the damage taken
credits.spritesNote: The Pokémon are the official battle sprites of {source} (No. 1–649 and the formes of their day), {license}, used in a non-commercial fan game only.
credits.custom: Pokémon sprites (No. 650 on, regional forms and more)
credits.customNote: The Pokémon and formes Black & White never drew are the {source}’s sprites in the same style, shared for fan projects with credit, with thanks to every artist below.
credits.trainers: Trainer sprites (leaders, Elite Four and champions never drawn in pixels)
credits.trainers.smogon: Kalos and Alola: the {source} community's fan sprites in Black & White's style, shared with credit.
credits.trainers.pokerogue: Grant, Diantha, Galar, Paldea and Blueberry: sprites from the fan game {source} ({license}); this game crops them and shares them on the same terms.
credits.trainers.showdown: Avery and Klara: {source}'s trainer sprites, by {artist}. Fan art shared on condition of credit and no edits; only the empty margin is trimmed.
credits.trainers.hns: Johto's and Kanto's leaders walking the road: from {source}, a fan remake of HeartGold and SoulSilver on Emerald's engine.
items.afterBattleNote: After a win, healing items from the bag top the companion up to this much health.
items.afterBattlePpNote: A move down to a quarter of its PP gets an Ether, one at a time, or an Elixir when no Ether is left.
